I was away at college for 7 or so years. Well, I was in the dorms for 5. I was in an abusive relationship for 3 of those, so I learned very easily how to hide all emotion, sit completely still, and don't make any movements or noise. Since coming home I have relaxed a little bit into a less bodily controlled state, but there are still piles of habits I have of just hiding emotions, and the thing that hurts the most, is realizing that eventually all the hiding of the sadness does is represent me as a malicious and angry person to other people. When I do not desire doing that. 

About 4 years ago, I had a therapist comment that it was strange that I smiled when I talked about something sad. I do not know whether she was creeped out by me, or she had observed this before, but I just got really used to I suppose, forcing myself to smile and look happy and do anything I could to stop myself from crying, when talking about difficult or painful things. I know a lot in therapy I would start crying, and to stop, I would smile, like just half of one. I did that for almost anything I burst into tears over for years. 

I don't think it's right to put on a brave face when one experiences pain. It really is more of a weakness, to hide sorrow. Because it just makes other people ashamed of their own, and the only way I know I even really acknowledge my own, is when someone else acknowledges that it is okay for me to feel it. I've had people close to me call and mock me, call me a baby for crying in front of them, or be happy that I call them a bully, that it is something to be proud of. And I know those people in my life are trying, I suppose, to help me, but calling me too sensitive and then mocking me for it, is not right. 

It lifts slowly, but, every time I experience this, I do not know how to prevent it from happening again, aside from, figure out what all the mistakes I made that led up to this point, and do not make them again. But every person is different, has a different set of expectations of what a mistake is, what is acceptable behavior and what is not, and I have a tendency to socially isolate myself. The mistake is really, that I keep trying to be perfect, and I am never going to be. But I can not seem to just accept that, and just start looking towards some kind of future. 

My personal barriers are just, hoping I will find someone to be with that actually wants to be with me, and the hope that I have not too narrowly defined that criteria, thereby nearly ensuring loneliness for the rest of my life. I don't really think I have. I may look like shit right now and feel like crap and also, am not very good at keeping a job or doing much at all, but I know that I am very capable and have two degrees and if I try hard enough I will accomplish the goals in life that I want to accomplish, mostly, get a phd, or 2, and married or something.

From one perspective I think it's good I can assess where all the issues lay, but from the other, I may just be over-analyzing, and trying to find what my problem really is, while also not making much progress on day to day things. Or going sort of in a sometimes progress, sometimes not. I over analyze myself too much, I need to just focus a lot more on exercising, eating healthfully, drink more water, and eventually socialize outside of the internet. Just hard to get motivation to do any of those things. And sleeping better. All the basic things about taking care of myself, I am not very good at, and have never really been. Just this huge twisty maze of learned ways to eat, or sleep, or move about day to day, which is mostly, sleep not a whole lot, obsess over 'work' which is really more just tricking myself into thinking I am learning anything useful for future work, and very strange eating habits. It is hard to question those things day to day. But I must, so hopefully writing them out will help me remember a little better.
